name: custom element
title: Custom element — author-defined element name containing a hyphen
description: Any element whose custom element name is a valid hyphenated name registered through customElements.define(). Names cannot be enumerated, so one primitive covers the whole family. Three variants exist and share the same naming rule; they differ only in the base class they extend and in the categories they gain.

dom.interface: HTMLElement (autonomous and form-associated) or the extended built-in interface (customized built-in), subclassed by the author

naming.rule: Valid custom element name: begins with [a-z], contains at least one hyphen, contains no uppercase ASCII letters, and is not a reserved hyphenated name (annotation-xml, color-profile, font-face, font-face-src, font-face-uri, font-face-format, font-face-name, missing-glyph).

content_categories.note: Applies to the autonomous and form-associated variants. A customized built-in element takes the categories of its built-in local name instead.

form_categories.note: Autonomous variant: none. Form-associated variant: see variants.form-associated. Customized built-in variant: those of the built-in local name.

syntax.children_note: Child content is governed by the element’s content model in its spec definition.
syntax.note: Applies to the autonomous and form-associated variants; a customized built-in element keeps the syntax kind of its built-in local name.

placement.note: Allowed wherever flow or phrasing content is expected, subject to the enclosing content model. A customized built-in element follows the placement of its built-in local name.

autonomous.title: Autonomous custom element
autonomous.description: Extends HTMLElement directly and is written with its own tag name.

form-associated.title: Form-associated custom element
form-associated.description: An autonomous custom element whose class sets static formAssociated = true. It gains a form owner through ElementInternals and joins the listed form categories in addition to the autonomous categories.
form-associated.interface: HTMLElement (author subclass with static formAssociated = true)
form-associated.note: Does not automatically gain autocapitalize-and-autocorrect-inheriting membership.
form-associated.example:
<form>
  <fancy-input name="nickname"></fancy-input>
</form>
<script>
  customElements.define("fancy-input", class extends HTMLElement {
    static formAssociated = true;
    #internals = this.attachInternals();
  });
</script>

customized-built-in.title: Customized built-in element
customized-built-in.description: Extends a built-in element’s interface and is used through the is="" attribute on the built-in tag. The hyphenated name is the is value; no new element name is introduced.
customized-built-in.interface: The built-in element’s interface (for example HTMLButtonElement), subclassed by the author
customized-built-in.content_categories: inherited from the built-in local name
customized-built-in.form_categories: inherited from the built-in local name
customized-built-in.form_associated: inherited from the built-in local name
customized-built-in.syntax: inherited from the built-in local name
customized-built-in.note: Use the classification of their built-in local name; is does not introduce a new element name.
customized-built-in.example:
<button is="fancy-button">Click</button>
<script>
  customElements.define("fancy-button", class extends HTMLButtonElement {}, { extends: "button" });
</script>
